constraints: @exharness/benchmark is private workspace infrastructure with a public package contract; it must not import packages/core-harness, packages/agentic-system, Harbor implementation code, provider SDKs, Blackboard controller code, or retired scripts/delivery/baseline implementation.
Harbor is pinned and isolated behind a benchmark substrate adapter. Harbor process/trial/verifier details may be captured as evidence but may not become package-internal semantics.
BB-065 calibrates benchmark infrastructure only: it does not compare ExHarness against another harness, select an async profile, or make a product-value conclusion.

Every started attempt remains represented. Quality is independently evaluated and orthogonal to termination/provider/infrastructure state; retries append new attempts and never overwrite earlier attempts.
Unknown token, cache or cost fields remain null with explicit UNKNOWN/PARTIAL status; missing observations are never converted to zero or success.

Deterministic local calibration is credential-free and model-free. External sanity uses only a bounded pinned workload with oracle/nop controls selected before downstream live model results are observed.
Legacy current execution paths are retired only after replacement package/substrate calibration passes. Historical evidence stays recoverable through Git and is not rewritten into the new objective.
invariants: Benchmark truth is independent from the system under measurement: @exharness/benchmark cannot depend on ExHarness product runtime, Harbor implementation, provider SDKs, Blackboard controller code, or retired baseline implementation.
Experiment/unit/fixed-factor identity is immutable after execution begins; every started attempt and retry remains append-only and evidence-bound.
Quality is owned only by the independent evaluator and remains orthogonal to termination, provider and infrastructure state; missing usage/cost stays nullable UNKNOWN/PARTIAL rather than zero.

Materialized evidence is authoritative for audit: candidate, evaluator, accounting and normalized outcomes must be recomputable from immutable evidence identities, and tampering or missing evidence fails closed.

BB-065 establishes infrastructure trust only; downstream harness economics, capability attribution, delivery value, improvement and release studies reuse the kernel but own their experiment-specific adapters/protocols.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Create packages/benchmark as private Node workspace package @exharness/benchmark. It exposes only the package root, supports no deep-import contract, and has no runtime dependencies in BB-065 beyond Node built-ins.

D2 — Public exports are exactly createExperimentRegistration, createBenchmarkUnit, AttemptLedger, normalizeOutcome, createEvidenceManifest, normalizeAccounting, auditAttempt, assertExperimentRegistration, assertBenchmarkUnit, assertAttemptRecord, assertEvidenceManifest, assertSubstratePort, CONTRACT_KINDS and OUTCOME_ENUMS.

D3 — Canonical schemas are EXPERIMENT_REGISTRATION_V1, BENCHMARK_UNIT_V1, ATTEMPT_LEDGER_EVENT_V1, BENCHMARK_ATTEMPT_RECORD_V1, EVIDENCE_MANIFEST_V1, ACCOUNTING_V1 and BENCHMARK_AUDIT_V1; experiment/unit/fixed-factor identities are immutable and digest-bound.

D4 — AttemptLedger is append-only: beginAttempt appends STARTED before substrate execution; settleAttempt appends SETTLED; retry creates a new attemptId with retryOfAttemptId; recovery may append a terminal observation but never overwrites history.

D5 — Package code enforces schema, identity, retry, orthogonal outcome, nullable accounting, evidence-digest and audit invariants. Adapters own real reset, process invocation, raw evidence collection, artifact extraction, evaluator invocation and truthful raw-to-normalized mapping.

D6 — Harbor v0.23.0 at commit 1e5c5c6db929a10a140d05e606882c671ae20729 is isolated under benchmarks/substrate/harbor/**. adapter.mjs implements SubstratePort around a pinned Harbor child process; harbor_agent.py is Harbor-facing and cannot be imported by packages/benchmark.

D7 — Failure mapping is fixed: ENV_BUILD for environment build; ENV_RUNTIME for environment runtime; ADAPTER_SETUP for custom-agent/bootstrap; HARNESS_PROTOCOL for missing/malformed trial contract; ARTIFACT_EXTRACTION for extraction; VERIFIER_ERROR + NOT_EVALUATED for verifier crash; AGENT_TIMEOUT for agent wall timeout; provider rate-limit/timeout/5xx remain providerStatus and do not synthesize quality.

D8 — Lifecycle is register experiment -> register units -> begin attempt -> prepare -> execute -> collect -> independent evaluate when evaluable -> normalize outcome/accounting -> settle -> fresh-process audit. Producer exit status never substitutes for evaluator quality.

D9 — Local calibration is credential-free/model-free. Four owned fixtures cover pass, artifact reopening, producer-success/verifier-fail and failure normalization. External sanity deterministically seals exactly two pinned Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks after oracle 5/5 + nop fail 1/1.

D10 — Legacy migration is replacement-before-delete: inventory consumers, apply explicit disposition matrix, build/calibrate replacement, cut root entrypoints, run forbidden-reference scan, then delete scripts/delivery/baseline/** and its test/delivery/** tests. Historical provenance remains only in Git.

D11 — BB-077 consumes only @exharness/benchmark public API plus BENCHMARK_SUBSTRATE_MANIFEST_V1 and owns DIRECT_CODEACT/CORE_SYNC adapters, fixed-factor protocol, economics metrics, cohort/repeats and comparison reducer. It cannot reimplement AttemptLedger/evidence/accounting truth.

D12 — BB-081, BB-074, BB-075 and BB-076 reuse the same experiment/unit/attempt/evidence/accounting backbone. Their metrics/gates remain experiment-owned; bypassing kernel attempt/evidence truth is a contract violation.
implementationSlices: S0 — Inventory and freeze legacy retirement: enumerate every current import/script/documented executable consumer of scripts/delivery/baseline/**; classify each as DROP, REIMPLEMENT_GENERIC or DOWNSTREAM_OWNER; materialize a deletion manifest and prove product runtime has no dependency on it.

S1 — Benchmark kernel: create packages/benchmark with the exact root exports/schemas in benchmarkPackageContract; implement immutable experiment/unit registration, canonical digests, append-only AttemptLedger, orthogonal Outcome, nullable Accounting and Port validators using Node built-ins only.

S2 — Harbor adapter: implement adapter.mjs + identity.mjs + harbor_agent.py; pin Harbor identity, spawn one trial per attempt, enforce fresh workspace/output identity, extract raw trial/artifact/verifier refs, and map failures exactly per harborAdapterContract without importing Harbor into the package.

S3 — Deterministic calibration: implement four credential-free fixtures and prove producer success + verifier fail, accepted artifact after budget exhaustion, provider timeout/no artifact, UNKNOWN usage, retry preservation, reset isolation and verifier/artifact failures.

S4 — Evidence and audit reopening: persist EVIDENCE_MANIFEST_V1, restart audit in a fresh process, reopen raw result/artifact/verifier/usage evidence, recompute normalized attempt/accounting digests and reject tampering, missing refs, identity drift or zero-filled unknown usage.

S5 — External sanity: use pinned Terminal-Bench 2.1; deterministically select two bundles after oracle 5/5 and nop fail 1/1, seal identities before downstream model results, perform no coding-model call, and emit BENCHMARK_SUBSTRATE_MANIFEST_V1.

S6 — Legacy retirement and downstream handoff: only after S1-S5 pass, cut retired root entrypoints, delete scripts/delivery/baseline/** and its test/delivery/** tests, run forbidden-reference scans, wire npm run test:benchmark, update Living benchmark and system state truth, and prove a BB-077 fixture imports only public kernel exports plus substrate manifest.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: @exharness/benchmark has the exact root exports, schemas, no-runtime-dependency rule and immutable identity semantics specified by the plan, with no downstream deep-import dependency.
Every started attempt is append-only, retry creates a new attempt linked by retryOfAttemptId, prior failures remain auditable, and experiment/unit/fixed-factor identities cannot change after start.
Harbor process/trial/reset/artifact/verifier behavior is owned entirely by the substrate adapter and normalized through SubstratePort; packages/benchmark has no Harbor-specific dependency or branch.
Independent verifier quality remains orthogonal to termination/provider/infrastructure state and the required truth-table cases normalize exactly without synthesizing quality from producer status.
Token/cache/cost observations are nullable and status-qualified; absent usage remains null/UNKNOWN or PARTIAL and can never be zero-filled as observed usage.
A fresh process reopens immutable evidence and deterministically recomputes candidate/evaluator/outcome/accounting identity; tampered, missing or mismatched evidence fails audit.

Exactly two pinned external sanity tasks are selected by preregistered digest order only after Harbor oracle 5/5 and nop fail 1/1, with task/environment identities sealed before downstream live results.

Every retired baseline capability has an explicit migration disposition, replacement calibration passes before deletion, no current executable reference remains, and historical evidence is not rewritten.
A BB-077 contract fixture uses only @exharness/benchmark public exports and the substrate manifest while owning DIRECT_CODEACT/CORE_SYNC and comparison-specific logic itself.
BB-065 changes no product-runtime source and emits no harness winner, async promotion, delivery-value or release decision.

negativeVerificationCases: packages/benchmark imports product runtime, Harbor implementation, provider SDK, Blackboard controller, or scripts/delivery/baseline and dependency-boundary still passes.
A downstream benchmark deep-imports packages/benchmark/src/** instead of the package root and the contract test still passes.
Experiment or unit fixed-factor identity changes after the first STARTED attempt and the ledger accepts it.
A retry success overwrites or removes the original failed attempt.
Producer SUCCESS with verifier FAIL becomes ACCEPTED.
A verified artifact after budget exhaustion is forced to REJECTED because termination was not COMPLETED.
Provider timeout with no evaluable artifact becomes REJECTED instead of NOT_EVALUATED.
Missing usage/cost/cache observation is written as zero or treated as KNOWN.
Verifier crash becomes REJECTED instead of NOT_EVALUATED + VERIFIER_ERROR.
A materialized artifact/result/verifier record is modified after settlement and audit still passes.
Harbor reuses workspace, trial id, candidate directory or evidence output path across attempts.
BB-077 bypasses AttemptLedger or reimplements benchmark accounting/evidence truth.
Retired scripts/delivery/baseline executable entrypoints or imports remain reachable after S6.
External sanity task selection changes after seeing downstream model outcomes.
BB-065 changes product runtime or emits a harness/value promotion decision.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: @exharness/benchmark exposes explicit Experiment, Unit, AttemptLedger, Outcome, Evidence, Accounting, Audit and Port contracts with immutable identity/fixed-factor rules, append-only retries, orthogonal outcomes, nullable accounting and deterministic reopening/audit.

A Harbor adapter outside packages/benchmark owns process invocation, trial identity, fresh workspace/reset, artifact/verifier extraction, raw evidence references and normalized substrate failure mapping while packages/benchmark remains Harbor-independent.

Deterministic calibration proves producer SUCCESS plus verifier FAIL is REJECTED; budget exhaustion plus a valid verified artifact is ACCEPTED with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED; provider timeout without an artifact is NOT_EVALUATED; missing usage remains UNKNOWN/null; retries preserve failed attempts; and tampered evidence fails audit.

The implementation boundary is concrete at file/API/test level and architectural negatives fail when packages/benchmark imports product runtime, Harbor or provider SDKs, when downstream work bypasses AttemptLedger, or when the retired baseline remains executable.

Legacy scripts/delivery/baseline capabilities are inventoried and explicitly mapped to DROP, reimplementation under the new generic contract, or downstream ownership before current entrypoints are removed.

BB-065 emits one reusable benchmark/evidence/accounting backbone and substrate manifest that BB-077, BB-081, BB-074, BB-075 and BB-076 can consume without inventing parallel experimental infrastructure.
